skills.name: fetch_available_agents
skills.description: Connects to Azure AI Foundry and retrieves all available agents registered in the project, then STRICTLY scopes the returned set to the prompt's domain. Uses a weighted keyword classifier (primary nouns/brand names ×3, secondary verbs ×1) to place both the prompt and each agent into one of the known domains (flights, hotels, food-delivery, dining, electronics). Only agents whose classified domain matches the prompt's domain are returned. If the prompt cannot be classified, only agents that are themselves domain-neutral (no classified domain) are returned — never a mismatched-domain agent. This is what prevents a laptop agent (e.g. Lenovo) from responding to a food prompt with hallucinated generic options.

input.prompt: The user prompt used to determine the target domain

skills.output: List of AgentInfo objects restricted to the prompt's domain (or the domain-neutral subset when the prompt has no classifiable domain). May be empty — the workflow will surface a clarification in that case.

domainContract.fallbackWhenPromptUnclassified: keep only agents whose ClassifyAgent returns an empty domain
domainContract.fallbackWhenAgentUnclassified: drop the agent whenever the prompt IS classified

skills.name: select_best_agent
skills.description: Ranks the domain-scoped agent set from fetch_available_agents against the user prompt, user preferences, and vector-store history. Applies a cross-domain hard penalty so a wrong-domain agent that slipped through the filter cannot win on incidental token overlap. Optionally hands the top candidates to a Foundry LLM (AzureFoundry:SelectorAgentId) for the final pick. Falls back to the heuristic ranking alone if no selector agent is configured or the call fails. Never returns an agent from a domain different from the prompt's domain.

input.userContext: User preferences, past interactions, and stored embeddings

skills.output: Ranked list of best-matching AgentInfo objects (max 5 for generic queries, capped further by workflow fan-out settings). Guaranteed same-domain as the prompt.
selectionCriteria: User's historical preference for specific providers (vector-store bonus)
Explicit brand mention in the prompt (narrows to that brand's agent when present)
Final LLM-assisted selection via AzureFoundry:SelectorAgentId, informed by heuristic scores

skills.name: execute_agent_action
skills.description: Invokes the selected Foundry agent via its MCP server endpoint. The agent MUST return concrete offers (JSON array under a ```json fence) with fields: title (the specific item / booking / itinerary identifier — e.g. "Margherita Pizza (12in)", "Booking #AA1234"), description (2-3 sentence detail of what the offer includes), price (number), currency. No hallucinated generic options — the agent must respond only about items/services it actually hosts. Clarification-only replies are dropped downstream by the ranker.

input.prompt: The enriched prompt with user context

skills.output: Structured response from the agent containing an array of {title, description, price, currency, ...attributes} — one entry per real offer the agent hosts. Title is short and specific to the item / booking / reservation number. Description is the agent-provided detail — no invented content.

skills.name: confirm_booking
skills.description: Sends a confirmation request to the selected agent's MCP server. The agent processes the booking through the provider's system (e.g., Air India, Emirates) and returns confirmation details including booking ID, itinerary, and status.
skills.output: ConfirmationDetails with booking ID, provider, and itinerary summary

skills.name: store_context_embedding
skills.description: Stores processed interaction data as vector embeddings in the user's personal vector store. This enables RAG-based retrieval for future interactions, allowing the system to remember preferences like preferred airlines, seat types, meal choices, and travel times.
skills.output: Confirmation that embedding was stored successfully
